text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on December 31 in history.
1491 - Jacques Cartier, French navigator who explored the North American coast and the St Lawrence river, born.
1600 - Queen Elizabeth I granted a charter to the "company of merchants of London trading to the East Indies" - the East India Company.
1719 - John Flamsteed, who became England's first Astronomer Royal, died; the Greenwich Observatory was built for him.

1720 - Charles Edward Stuart (Bonnie Prince Charlie), claimant to the British throne and leader of the Jacobite rebellion, born in Rome. The cause of the "Young Pretender" suffered a fatal blow in 1746 with his defeat by the English army at Culloden Moor.
1869 - Henri Matisse, French painter and sculptor, born.

1880 - George Marshall, U.S. general and statesman, born. Chief of staff (1939-1945), he directed the U.S. army during World War Two. As Secretary of State (1947-1949), he devised the Marshall Plan for Europe's post-war reconstruction.
1911 - Marie Curie received her second Nobel prize for her work on radioactive elements.
1937 - Welsh actor Anthony Hopkins born; he won the Oscar for best actor for "The Silence of the Lambs".
1938 - Dr R.N. Harger's "drunkometer", the first breath test for car drivers, was officially introduced in Indianapolis.
1948 - Sir Malcolm Campbell, British racing driver, died. He broke land speed records nine times and in 1935 in Utah he became the first to travel on land at over 300 miles (483 km) per hour.
1968 - Russia's TU-144 supersonic airliner made its first flight, several months ahead of the Anglo-French Concorde which it closely resembled.
1971 - Austrian Kurt Waldheim took over as U.N. Secretary-General after U Thant retired.
1973 - A three-day work week was introduced in Britain to conserve energy during a miners' strike.
1981 - In Ghana, President Hilla Limann's civilian government was overthrown in a military coup led by Flight Lieutenant Jerry Rawlings.
1994 - Bosnia's Moslem-led government signed an agreement for a four-month ceasefire in Bosnia, the 1,000th day of the bitter Serb siege of Sarajevo.
1995 - Algerian President Liamine Zeroual appointed Ahmed Ouyahia as prime minister to replace Mokdad Sifi.
